notes: DEPLOYED-BINARY GUARD (scope 1+2) — tools/smoke.sh is now wired into `zig build test` (build.zig test step, same gate as the pre-commit and resume regressions; precedent build.zig precommit_regression). Staleness is an ERROR, not a warning: T268 built a real check that never ran (T286's window left the project with no read-first surface), and a warning inside a passing suite is the same silence. ORDERING-TRAP RULING: option (c) of the brief — fail only when the deployed binary is older than a COMMITTED source change. Implementation in smoke.sh: per-tool source scope (the tool's src, tools/gen-version.sh, build.zig); a bin/ tool FAILS iff its embedded build commit is missing/unstamped, not an ancestor of HEAD, or `git log <built>..HEAD -- <sources>` is non-empty. Uncommitted edits never trip it (HEAD unchanged), so a normal edit-test cycle does not break — the guard bites exactly when a cold reader could be misled (T286's shape: source change committed, deploy skipped). TRADE-OFF stated: build.zig is in every tool's scope, so a committed build.zig edit flags every tool until `zig build deploy` (one command); chose the loud side — both T268 and T286 were deploy-skips, and a build.zig edit can alter any binary's build or deploy recipe. Why it still catches T286: bin/managent was e370b26 while the resume subcommand was committed source; git log e370b26..HEAD -- src/managent non-empty → FAIL, independent of zig-out (the old bin==zig-out rule only failed when zig-out had been refreshed, which was exactly the case that slipped).
